rounds.proof_sketch: blockDim.y = 1 in 1D launch config. Mutated loop: each thread writes positions tid, tid+1, tid+2, ... creating races. However, all threads compute identical output values: inv_batch_sum from shared warp_sums[0] (synced), input[pos] from same global memory. Race condition is benign - all competing writes carry identical value.
rounds.survival_reason: The kernel is launched with a 1D block configuration (<<<16, 256>>>), making blockDim.y default to 1. The mutated loop 'for (int i = tid; i < dim; i += 1)' causes each thread to process almost all elements (thread 0 processes all 16384, thread 255 processes 16129). This creates race conditions where multiple threads write to the same output positions. However, since all threads read from the same shared memory value (warp_sums[0]) after synchronization and the same global memory (input[pos]), every thread computes and writes the identical value to each position. The race condition is therefore benign - regardless of which thread's write is observed, the value is correct.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable. The mutation changes iteration stride from 256 to 1, creating benign race conditions where all racing writes carry identical values. No value pattern can produce different outputs because the computation is deterministic and all threads compute the same result for each element.
rounds.recommendations: When testing CUDA kernels with redundant write patterns (multiple threads writing to same location), verify that all racing writes carry semantically identical values. Mutations that change stride patterns may create races but remain equivalent if the computed values are deterministic across all participating threads.
